sources.name: USGS Earthquake Hazards Program
sources.attribution: Earthquake data: U.S. Geological Survey (USGS)
sources.expected_latency: Automatic solutions typically within minutes; reviewed solutions hours to days later

coverage.geographic: Global (M4.5+ worldwide; smaller events primarily in the U.S. and territories)
coverage.temporal: Real-time feeds: past hour to past 30 days. FDSN catalog: 1900 to present

sources.resolution: Point hypocentres; location uncertainty typically 1–10 km
sources.historical_depth: ComCat catalog via FDSN event web service
sources.rate_limits: No published hard limit. Summary feeds are CDN-cached; ATLAS polls once per minute and uses conditional requests.

reliability.rationale: Authoritative national seismic network with global coverage and reviewed solutions

limitations: Magnitudes and locations of 'automatic' events are routinely revised.
Small events outside the U.S. are not catalogued in real time.
PAGER alert levels are estimates of shaking-related losses, not observations.

sources.name: GDACS — Global Disaster Alert and Coordination System
sources.provider: European Commission Joint Research Centre & UN OCHA

license.name: Creative Commons Attribution (CC BY)
license.notes: GDACS states its information is indicative and must not be used for decision making without alternate sources.

sources.attribution: Alerts: GDACS (European Commission JRC & UN OCHA), CC BY
sources.expected_latency: Earthquake alerts typically within 30 minutes of origin; cyclone alerts per advisory cycle
sources.resolution: Event centroids, wind-buffer and affected-area polygons where published
sources.historical_depth: Archive back to 2000s via SEARCH endpoint
sources.rate_limits: No published limit. ATLAS polls every 10 minutes and fetches geometry only for changed events.
sources.cache_strategy: TTL 9 min for event list; geometry cached per episode

reliability.rationale: Inter-agency system; alert levels are model-based impact estimates

limitations: Alert levels are automated impact-model estimates (MODEL provenance), not damage observations.
GDACS earthquake parameters are derived from NEIC/USGS and are not independent confirmation.
Wildfire and drought events are aggregated from GWIS and GDO respectively.

sources.name: NASA EONET — Earth Observatory Natural Event Tracker

license.name: NASA open data (no restrictions); constituent sources retain their terms

sources.attribution: Natural events: NASA EONET
sources.update_interval: Varies by upstream source (minutes to days)
sources.expected_latency: Curated metadata; hours for most categories
sources.resolution: Point or polygon per observation date
sources.historical_depth: Closed events queryable by date range
sources.rate_limits: No published limit. ATLAS polls every 20 minutes.

reliability.rationale: Curated aggregator; quality depends on the referenced primary source

limitations: Wildfire events are dominated by U.S. (IRWIN/InciWeb) and Canadian sources.
Magnitude fields are source-specific (kts for storms, acres for fires).

sources.name: NASA FIRMS — Active Fire Detections (VIIRS & MODIS)
sources.attribution: We acknowledge the use of data from the NASA LANCE FIRMS (https://earthdata.nasa.gov/firms), part of the NASA Earth Science Data and Information System (ESDIS).
sources.update_interval: Continuous as satellite overpasses are processed; ATLAS refreshes every 30 minutes
sources.expected_latency: Near-real-time: typically within 3 hours of satellite overpass

coverage.temporal: Public files: last 24 h / 48 h / 7 days

sources.historical_depth: Archive back to 2000 (MODIS) / 2012 (VIIRS) via the MAP_KEY API or archive download
sources.rate_limits: Public global CSV files require no key. Optional MAP_KEY API is subject to a per-key transaction quota.
sources.cache_strategy: TTL 25 min, ETag revalidation (files are ~1–8 MB)

reliability.rationale: Standard NASA active-fire product with documented algorithms

limitations: A detection marks a pixel containing one or more thermal anomalies, not a fire perimeter.
Near-real-time data does not distinguish vegetation fires from gas flares, volcanoes or industrial heat.
Cloud and smoke obscure detections; absence of detections is not absence of fire.
Fire clusters and their areas are ATLAS-derived groupings of detections.

sources.name: NOAA National Hurricane Center — Active Storms
sources.attribution: Tropical cyclone advisories: NOAA National Hurricane Center
sources.update_interval: Every 6 hours (3-hourly intermediate advisories during watches/warnings)

coverage.geographic: Atlantic, Eastern and Central Pacific basins

sources.resolution: Advisory point positions; forecast cones published as GIS
sources.rate_limits: No published limit. ATLAS polls every 15 minutes.

reliability.rationale: Official WMO Regional Specialized Meteorological Centre for its basins

limitations: Covers NHC/CPHC basins only; other basins come from GDACS and EONET.
Forecast tracks and cones are forecasts by NHC, not certainties.

sources.name: Smithsonian / USGS Weekly Volcanic Activity Report
sources.provider: Smithsonian Institution Global Volcanism Program & USGS

license.name: Public domain (product of U.S. Government employees); citation requested

sources.attribution: Global Volcanism Program, Weekly Volcanic Activity Report. Smithsonian Institution and US Geological Survey.
sources.rate_limits: No published limit. ATLAS polls every 6 hours.

reliability.rationale: Curated reports compiled from volcano observatories

limitations: Weekly cadence: not suitable for real-time eruption alerting.
Reports summarise observatory statements; consult the local observatory for alerts.

sources.name: NASA GIBS — Global Imagery Browse Services
sources.attribution: Imagery: NASA Global Imagery Browse Services (GIBS), part of NASA ESDIS
sources.update_interval: Daily (most products); sub-daily for some (e.g. IMERG 30-min)
sources.historical_depth: Full mission archive per layer, time-addressable via WMTS TIME dimension
sources.rate_limits: Tiles are CDN-served; no key required.
sources.cache_strategy: Browser HTTP cache; tiles requested only for the visible viewport

reliability.rationale: Operational NASA imagery service

limitations: Visualisations are rendered images, not calibrated science data values.

sources.name: EOxCloudless — Sentinel-2 cloudless mosaic (2024)
sources.provider: EOX IT Services GmbH (contains modified Copernicus Sentinel data)

license.name: Free for non-commercial use with attribution (EOX licence terms)
license.notes: Commercial deployments require a licence from EOX. ATLAS loads these tiles in the browser only; nothing is redistributed.

sources.attribution: EOxCloudless https://cloudless.eox.at by EOX IT Services GmbH (Contains modified Copernicus Sentinel data 2024)
sources.rate_limits: Public WMTS; tiles requested only for the visible viewport

reliability.rationale: Widely used cloud-free basemap from Copernicus Sentinel-2

limitations: A cloud-free composite of many dates: it shows typical surface appearance, not current conditions.

sources.name: Natural Earth — Admin-0 countries & populated places
sources.attribution: Made with Natural Earth
sources.rate_limits: Downloaded once during setup

reliability.rationale: Widely used cartographic reference

limitations: Boundaries reflect de facto control as mapped by Natural Earth and are not an endorsement of any claim.
Generalised geometry: points within a few km of a border may be attributed to the neighbouring country.

sources.name: Open-Meteo Forecast API

license.name: CC BY 4.0 (data); free API for non-commercial use

sources.attribution: Weather data by Open-Meteo.com (CC BY 4.0)

coverage.temporal: Forecast up to 16 days; archive since 1940 (ERA5)

sources.resolution: 1–11 km depending on the underlying weather model
sources.historical_depth: ERA5 reanalysis back to 1940 via the archive API
sources.rate_limits: 10,000 calls/day on the free tier. ATLAS fetches per incident on demand and caches 30 minutes.

reliability.rationale: Aggregates national weather models; values are model output

limitations: All values are numerical weather model output (MODEL provenance), not station observations.

sources.name: ReliefWeb API v2

license.name: Per-document terms; API terms of use apply

sources.attribution: Humanitarian reports: ReliefWeb (UN OCHA) and original publishers
sources.rate_limits: 1,000 calls/day per appname

reliability.rationale: Curated humanitarian information service

limitations: Since v2, requests without a pre-approved appname are rejected (HTTP 403). Disabled until configured.

sources.name: OpenAQ v3
sources.attribution: Air quality data: OpenAQ and contributing providers
sources.rate_limits: 60/min, 2,000/hour per free key

reliability.rationale: Aggregated reference and low-cost sensors

limitations: v3 requires a free API key. Disabled until configured.

sources.name: OpenStreetMap via Overpass API
sources.attribution: © OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL)
sources.rate_limits: Public instance: small number of concurrent slots per IP; heavy use must self-host.

reliability.rationale: Crowd-sourced; completeness varies strongly by country

limitations: Absence of a mapped facility does not mean the facility does not exist.

sources.name: GHSL GHS-POP R2023A (2025 epoch, 30 arc-second)
sources.attribution: Schiavina M. et al. (2023): GHS-POP R2023A. European Commission, Joint Research Centre (JRC)
sources.rate_limits: Single ~484 MB download (optional Population Pack)

reliability.rationale: Peer-reviewed global population grid

limitations: Population grids are modelled estimates (MODEL provenance) disaggregated from census data.
Exposure counts are residential population; daytime and seasonal populations differ.

sources.name: Terrain Tiles (Terrarium) on AWS Open Data
sources.provider: Mapzen / Linux Foundation (tilezen) on the AWS Open Data Sponsorship Program

license.name: Mixed open licences per source (see attribution list)

sources.attribution: Terrain: Terrain Tiles on AWS Open Data. USGS 3DEP, GMTED2010 and SRTM; NOAA ETOPO1; Copernicus EU-DEM; ArcticDEM; Geoscience Australia; Natural Resources Canada; INEGI; LINZ; Kartverket; UK Environment Agency; offene Daten Österreichs

coverage.temporal: Static composite of the listed DEMs

sources.resolution: ≈ 19 m at the zoom 13 used by ATLAS (source DEMs 1 m – 1 km)
sources.rate_limits: Public S3 bucket; requested only for visible tiles while 3D terrain is on
sources.cache_strategy: Decoded tiles kept in an in-memory LRU in the browser (384 tiles)

reliability.rationale: Static community dataset on AWS; no SLA

limitations: Heights below sea level are clamped to 0 m in ATLAS so imagery is never draped over bathymetry.
Source resolution varies strongly by country.
Visual relief only: not suitable for engineering or hydrological analysis.

sources.name: Sentinel-2 L2A via Earth Search (STAC) and AWS COGs
sources.provider: Element 84 (STAC API) · ESA Copernicus (Sentinel-2) · AWS Open Data

license.name: Copernicus Sentinel data terms (free, full and open)

sources.attribution: Contains modified Copernicus Sentinel data, processed by ATLAS. Catalogue: Element 84 Earth Search on AWS Open Data
sources.update_interval: New scenes within hours of acquisition; each place revisited about every 5 days
sources.expected_latency: Hours to a day after acquisition
sources.resolution: 10 m (visible, NIR) and 20 m (SWIR, scene classification)
sources.rate_limits: Public STAC API and public COG bucket; ATLAS reads small windows around one incident, on demand
sources.cache_strategy: Analysis results cached on disk for 24 h per incident and index

reliability.rationale: Operational ESA mission; widely used public catalogue

limitations: Clouds, cloud shadows, smoke and snow hide the surface; masked pixels are excluded and the valid fraction is reported.
Change between two dates also reflects season, harvest, tides and illumination, not only the hazard.
Index thresholds are published conventions (USGS dNBR classes, MNDWI > 0) and are not calibrated for every landscape.

sources.name: EMSC-CSEM earthquakes (FDSN event service)
sources.attribution: Earthquake data: EMSC-CSEM (European-Mediterranean Seismological Centre), CC BY 4.0
sources.update_interval: Real time (automatic solutions revised within minutes)

coverage.geographic: Global; densest in the Euro-Mediterranean region

sources.rate_limits: Polled every 5 min for the last 24 h, M ≥ 4.0

reliability.rationale: Established seismological agency; independent of USGS

limitations: Automatic solutions are revised; magnitude types (mb, Mw, ML) differ from USGS for the same event.
Incident threshold M ≥ 4.5, as for USGS; smaller events corroborate only.

sources.name: NOAA Tsunami Warning Centers (NTWC & PTWC)
sources.provider: NOAA National Weather Service — National Tsunami Warning Center and Pacific Tsunami Warning Center
sources.attribution: Tsunami messages: NOAA National Tsunami Warning Center and Pacific Tsunami Warning Center (tsunami.gov)

coverage.geographic: Messages for U.S. and Pacific/Caribbean areas of responsibility; information statements for large global events

sources.rate_limits: Two small Atom feeds polled every 3 min

reliability.rationale: Official warning authority

limitations: ATLAS links to the official bulletin and never rewrites tsunami guidance.
Other national tsunami warning systems (Japan, Indonesia, Chile, India…) are not yet ingested; always follow your national authority.

sources.name: NOAA Space Weather Prediction Center — NOAA scales
sources.provider: NOAA National Weather Service — Space Weather Prediction Center
sources.attribution: Space weather: NOAA Space Weather Prediction Center (SWPC)
sources.resolution: NOAA R, S and G scales (0–5)
sources.rate_limits: One small JSON, cached 10 min, fetched when the overview is open

reliability.rationale: Official space weather authority

limitations: Shown as context on the overview, not as incidents: geomagnetic storms have no single location.
The outlook is SWPC's forecast, quoted as issued; ATLAS adds no prediction.

sources.name: CelesTrak — NORAD two-line element sets

license.name: Free public data (derived from U.S. Space Force public catalog)

sources.attribution: Orbits: CelesTrak (NORAD two-line elements)
sources.rate_limits: Please do not request the same data more than every 2 hours; ATLAS caches for 6 h

reliability.rationale: Long-standing public orbital data service

limitations: Ground tracks and overpass times are predictions from public orbits (a few km accuracy for days); whether an image is actually taken depends on each mission's acquisition plan and on clouds.

sources.name: Copernicus DEM GLO-30 (AWS Open Data)
sources.provider: European Space Agency / Copernicus (data © DLR, Airbus)
sources.attribution: Copernicus DEM GLO-30 © DLR e.V. 2010–2014 and © Airbus Defence and Space GmbH 2014–2018, provided under COPERNICUS by the European Union and ESA
sources.rate_limits: One pixel read per right-click (cached)

reliability.rationale: Official Copernicus product on AWS Open Data

limitations: A surface model: heights include buildings and trees.
Land only: open water has no tile.
